subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should route/ACP bindings become a supported tool-policy enforcement layer, or should this need be routed to existing group/sender/session policy surfaces?
rationale: This adds a new config and authorization boundary; accepting the field without enforcement is unsafe, while enforcing it changes policy precedence across routing, ACP, embedded tools, and gateway tools.

options.title: Design binding-scoped policy
options.body: Approve a complete `bindings[].tools` contract with schema/types, matched-binding propagation, policy precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Use existing policy surfaces
options.body: Keep binding schemas closed and document per-agent, group/channel, and `toolsBySender` policies as the supported way to narrow tool access.

options.title: Fold into broader auth work
options.body: Defer this narrow feature to the broader per-session or conversation-identity authorization design so one security model owns the behavior.

recommendation.title: Design binding-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Approve a complete `bindings[].tools` contract with schema/types, matched-binding propagation, policy precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged scoped capability foundation and the adjacent product/security issues this decision depends on.
